notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found for the phrase order at 85). §1985:IX.4.3.2 prints DELETE file-name-1 RECORD, then [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ], then [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 ], then [ END-DELETE ], and §1985:IV.2.1 makes that sequence the format: "A general format is the specific arrangement of the elements of a clause or a statement." The one superset rule deleteStatement (RECORD and KEY optional words, END-DELETE optional) with the shared conditionalPhrases loop accepts the 1985 format, BindDelete binds it for every edition, and the later editions' additions are refused at 85 on recognition: the RETRY phrase by VisitRetryPhrase (COBOL0900), DELETE FILE by VisitDeleteFileStatement (COBOL0900), a second INVALID KEY or an AT END phrase by the association predicate (COBOL2269, COBOL0001). What is NOT implemented is the printed sequence of the two phrases: conditionalPhrases is ({conditionalPhraseAssociates($ctx)}? conditionalPhrase)* and ConditionalPhraseAssociation.Associates / MayAssociate test only that a phrase is printed by a format of the statement and not yet written, with no edition arm for the order, so NOT INVALID KEY written before INVALID KEY compiles at --std 85. The either-order reading is a 2002 change (§2002:F.2 item 33: "The conditional phrases in the ACCEPT, ADD, CALL, COMPUTE, DELETE, DISPLAY, DIVIDE, MULTIPLY, READ, RECEIVE, REWRITE, START, STRING, SUBTRACT, UNSTRING, and WRITE statements may be specified in any order."), and the row's own change record names it as what 2023 accepts and 1985 refuses. The mechanism is shared by every statement of that list (one grammar rule, one predicate); the sibling rows of this slice (READ, REWRITE, START, WRITE) carry the same finding. The witness runs the printed order only (INVALID KEY then NOT INVALID KEY, with END-DELETE, on a present and an absent key).

next.reason: 1985: "DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 ]"; 2023: "DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [ retry-phrase ] ┌ │ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 │ … NOT INVALID KEY … │ ┘ (choice indicators)". Same record format, but 2023 adds an optional retry-phrase. Its choice indicators also allow INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY in either order, so it accepts programs 1985 refuses.
